EPAR text-extracted (copyright EMEA 2007). Draft quote verbatim (p.52). Vasculitis sentence verbatim (p.11): 'Most monkeys with perivascular sheathing were positive for antibodies towards ranibizumab, indicating an immune-related effect which has not been observed clinically.' Also: 'it was suggested that an early onset of perivascular sheathing could be a marker for a later severe inflammatory response' and 'Therefore, the perivascular sheathing does not appear to be a useful marker for prediction of severe cases of inflammation in patients.' The monkey finding was proposed as a predictive marker and the regulator records it failed in patients; the brief's contra ('predicted wrongly', overrides matched) has no false-positive carve-out, so contra 2007. Swap the supporting quote to the 'has not been observed clinically' sentence. Facts in the draft are all correct; this is a rules call (rule questions #1, #4).

rule_questions: #1 False-positive safety signals: does contra ('the model predicted wrongly') cover a tox-species finding (ADA-linked perivascular sheathing/vasculitis in cynomolgus, EMA 2007) that the regulator attributed to exaggerated dosing of a human protein and that never appeared in patients? The brief has no carve-out, so I scored contra 2007; a carve-out would restore same 2007 and leave Karle 2023 as the sole contra.

#2 Dose magnitude threshold: label s12.3 states 3 d (animal) vs 9 d (human), a 3x miss in the conservative direction, while the operative monthly-dosing prediction held. The v2 magnitude/source_calls_it fields imply record-not-flip, so same stands; confirm that an off_by_2-5x PK parameter with the regimen holding is same, not contra.

#3 Juxtaposed comparisons: rule 1 requires a primary source that 'makes the comparison', but v2's comparison_stated=false explicitly permits self-juxtaposition. engagement 2006 and efficacy 2006 are both juxtaposed (label/MARINA vs Krzystolik 2002). Strict rule 1 -> untested; v2 reading -> same. Which governs?

#4 EMA EPAR admissibility: rule 1 lists peer-reviewed papers, FDA label/review, registry records; the EMA scientific discussion is not listed. The 2007 safety entry and model_filed rest on it. If disallowed, the substitute is the (image-only) FDA PharmR above, not Rosenfeld 2006, which contains no model comparison.

#5 Second contra entry: if 2007 flips to contra, the 2023 brolucizumab entry is not a change of status. Does 'one entry per change of status' drop it, or is a second contra instance (true false-negative vs 2007 false-positive) retained?
